title: FIRE and the 4% rule

sections.body: FIRE stands for Financial Independence, Retire Early. The idea: save and invest enough that your investments can cover your living costs, so work becomes optional.
Your FIRE number ≈ yearly spending × 25. Spend $40,000 a year and you'd aim for about $1,000,000 invested.

The ×25 comes from the 4% rule: withdraw 4% of your portfolio in year one, then adjust that amount for inflation each year. Historical US studies found this lasted at least 30 years in most past market periods.

items: It's a rule of thumb, not a guarantee. Future returns may differ from the past.
Retiring very early means your money may need to last 40 to 50 years, so many people plan with a lower rate, like 3.5%.
Cutting spending helps twice: you need a smaller FIRE number and you can save more toward it.

quiz.q: Using the 4% rule, what's the FIRE number for $50,000 of yearly spending?
Why might an early retiree use a withdrawal rate lower than 4%?
options: Their money may need to last more than 30 years
quiz.why: The 4% rule was tested over about 30 years. Longer retirements carry more risk.

quiz.q: How does cutting yearly spending affect your FIRE plan?
options: Lowers your FIRE number and frees money to invest
quiz.why: Lower spending shrinks the target and boosts your savings, a double win.

disclaimer: Educational content only, not financial advice. Past results don't guarantee future returns.
